title: Lactose intolerance: decreased stool pH (bacterial fermentation)
vignette: A 60-year-old woman comes to the office with intermittent flatulence, crampy abdominal pain, and watery diarrhea. Her symptoms started 2 months ago after she recovered from an episode of acute gastroenteritis associated with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. The patient's symptoms are worse after drinking "too much milk." She usually has 1 or 2 glasses of wine every evening with dinner. Physical examination is unremarkable. Initial laboratory evaluation, including serum chemistries, blood counts, stool cultures, and studies for ova and parasites, is negative. Which of the following is most likely decreased in this patient?

clues.text: symptoms started 2 months ago after she recovered from an episode of acute gastroenteritis
clues.note: Post-infectious (secondary) lactase deficiency follows mucosal injury from gastroenteritis - transiently reducing brush-border lactase.

clues.text: symptoms are worse after drinking "too much milk."
clues.note: Flatulence, cramps, and osmotic (watery) diarrhea worsening with dairy indicate LACTOSE INTOLERANCE (lactase deficiency).

clues.text: including serum chemistries, blood counts, stool cultures, and studies for ova and parasites, is negative
clues.note: A negative infectious/inflammatory workup supports a functional carbohydrate-malabsorption cause (lactose intolerance).

whatMatters: Post-gastroenteritis LACTOSE INTOLERANCE (secondary lactase deficiency): undigested lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria into short-chain fatty acids (acetate, butyrate, propionate) that ACIDIFY the stool - so STOOL pH is DECREASED. Answer E. (Breath hydrogen and stool osmolality are INCREASED.)
strategy: Trace the pathophysiology: lactase deficiency -> undigested lactose reaches the colon -> bacterial fermentation makes gas (increased breath H2) + short-chain fatty acids (LOWER stool pH) and osmotically active fragments (increased stool osmolality -> osmotic diarrhea). The question asks what DECREASES -> stool pH. Reject increased findings (breath hydrogen, stool osmolality) and unrelated pancreatic tests (fecal fat, pancreatic enzymes) - fat malabsorption/pancreatic enzymes aren't affected by lactase deficiency.

eliminations.label: Breath hydrogen content - INCREASED
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hydrogen gas produced when colonic bacteria ferment undigested lactose. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: breath hydrogen is INCREASED in lactose intolerance (basis of the hydrogen breath test), not decreased. ✅ Correct if: asking what INCREASES (diagnostic test).

eliminations.label: Fecal fat - normal (not a fat problem)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: stool fat content, elevated in FAT malabsorption/steatorrhea (e.g., pancreatic insufficiency, celiac). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: lactase deficiency impairs CARBOHYDRATE, not fat, digestion, so fecal fat is normal. ✅ Correct if: fat malabsorption (steatorrhea).

eliminations.label: Pancreatic enzymes - unaffected
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: exocrine pancreatic enzyme output (reduced in chronic pancreatitis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: secondary lactase deficiency is a brush-border problem, not pancreatic; pancreatic enzymes are unaffected. ✅ Correct if: exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

eliminations.label: Stool osmolality - INCREASED
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the osmotic load in stool. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: undigested lactose (and its fragments) raise stool osmolality, drawing water into the lumen (osmotic diarrhea) - so it is INCREASED, not decreased. ✅ Correct if: asking what INCREASES (osmotic gap).

reasoning: Post-gastroenteritis worsening with milk = secondary lactase deficiency (lactose intolerance)
Undigested lactose reaches the colon and is fermented by bacteria
Fermentation produces short-chain fatty acids that ACIDIFY the stool
-> stool pH is decreased; answer E
mechanism: Lactase, a brush-border enzyme of the small-intestinal villi, hydrolyzes lactose into glucose and galactose for absorption. LACTASE DEFICIENCY may be primary (lactase nonpersistence, common in Asian/African populations) or SECONDARY (acquired) - as here, from mucosal injury after INFECTIOUS gastroenteritis (also bacterial overgrowth, celiac disease) that damages the brush border. Undigested lactose is osmotically active, drawing water into the lumen (raising STOOL OSMOLALITY and causing OSMOTIC, watery diarrhea), and it passes into the colon where bacteria FERMENT it. This fermentation (1) produces gases including HYDROGEN (raising BREATH HYDROGEN, the basis of the hydrogen breath test) and (2) generates SHORT-CHAIN FATTY ACIDS (acetate, butyrate, propionate) that ACIDIFY the stool - DECREASING STOOL pH. Clinically: flatulence, bloating, cramps, and watery diarrhea after dairy, with a normal infectious/inflammatory workup; symptoms resolve with lactose avoidance or lactase supplements. Thus, among the choices, the DECREASED value is stool pH (breath hydrogen and stool osmolality increase; fecal fat and pancreatic enzymes are unaffected since fat/pancreatic digestion is intact).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid GI > lactose intolerance: lactase deficiency (primary/secondary); undigested lactose -> osmotic diarrhea; bacterial fermentation -> ↑breath hydrogen, ↑stool osmolality, and ↓stool pH (short-chain fatty acids).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Fermentation acidifies stool (↓pH); breath hydrogen and stool osmolality INCREASE.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on lactase deficiency, osmotic diarrhea, short-chain fatty acids, hydrogen breath test, or stool osmotic gap? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Breath hydrogen and stool osmolality are INCREASED; fecal fat/pancreatic enzymes are unaffected (carbohydrate, not fat/pancreatic, problem).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: lactose intolerance -> ↓stool pH, ↑breath hydrogen, ↑stool osmolality; osmotic diarrhea; treat with lactose avoidance/lactase.

keywords.back: Stool pH (bacterial fermentation -> short-chain fatty acids)

GI > fecal fat (fat malabsorption), pancreatic enzymes (pancreatic causes).

memoryHook: Colon bacteria ferment the leftover milk sugar into acids - so the stool turns acidic (low pH), the breath fills with hydrogen, and water floods in (osmotic diarrhea).
